name: Silk Road Trade Networks
region: Eurasia (China, Central Asia, Persia, Mediterranean, India)
summary: Overland and maritime trade network spanning Eurasia that exchanged goods, technologies, religions, and diseases across civilisational boundaries for 1600 years.

claims.statement: The Silk Road transmitted not just goods but technologies (papermaking, gunpowder, printing) and numeral systems between civilisations
No single empire controlled the full route — trade persisted through the fall of Rome, Han, Kushan, Sassanid, and Mongol dynasties
Caravanserai infrastructure created a decentralised logistics network with standardised rest stops every 30-40 km

evidence.source: Liu (2010) The Silk Road in World History, Oxford UP
Hansen (2012) The Silk Road: A New History, Oxford UP
Whitfield (2018) Silk, Slaves, and Stupas: Material Culture of the Silk Road, University of California Press
Hillenbrand (1994) Islamic Architecture: Form, Function, and Meaning — chapter on caravanserai networks

notes: The ultimate I/O bus of the pre-modern world. Technology transfer along this network directly enabled arabic_numerals reaching Europe and papermaking reaching the Islamic world. Cross-links with multiple domains.
